Testimony of Rep. Allison Hepler presenting
LD 2024, An Act to Make Changes to Certain Licensing Laws
Governing For-hire Charter Boat Operators, Lobster and Crab Fishing and Elver Dealers
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Marine Resources
Good aftemoon, Senator Tepler and colleagues of the Marine Resources Committee. I am
Allison Hepler and I represent the towns of Arrowsic, Georgetown, Phippsburg, West Bath and
Woolwich. I am pleased to introduce LD 2024, An Act to Make Changes to Certain Licensing
Laws Governing For-hire Charter Boat Operators, Lobster and Crab Fishing and Elver
Dealers.
This is the Department of Marine Resources' "technical changes bill." Some of the proposed legislation clarifies laws that we enacted last year, such as eligibility requirements for the "forhire charter boat license," as well as penalties related to elver dealers who have been convicted of an elver-related violation. The bill also eliminates the civil penalty for exceeding the lobster
trap limit, while retaining the criminal penalty.
As always, department bill-related questions are best left to the department but I am happy to try my best. Thank you!

Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Marine
Resources, my name is Deirdre Gilbert, I am Director of State Marine Policy at the Maine Department of Marine Resources, and l am testifying on behalf ofthe Department support of LD 2024. This is a Department bill and we are grateful to Representative Hepler for sponsoring it on our behalf.
LD 2024 represents the Department's "technical changes" bill for this legislative session, making minor clarifying changes to marine resources statutes. Specifically LD 2024:
0 Clarifies eligibility requirements for the "for-hire charter boat license" created last session.
Specifically, the Department is proposing amended language to better capture what license an
individual who does not hold a tidewater guide's license issued by lFW must hold. Based on further discussions with Marine Patrol, the following is their recommended language:
Possesses o valid United States Merchant Mariner Credential issued by the United States Coast Guard indicating an endorsement authorizing the individual to carry passengers for hire.
Q Under current law, there are two penalties provided for exceeding the lobster trap limit. LD 2024 seeks to eliminate the civil penalty and retain the existing criminal penalty, which is what these violations are typically written under. The criminal penalty also carries a mandatory
suspension, while the civil penalty does not. This will avoid two license holders who commit
the same violation from being charged differently, depending on which section of law they are
written under.
0 It removes a prohibition on issuing an elver dealer's license or supplemental license to a person
using the same business address as a person who has violated certain laws governing elver
dealers for at least 5 years following the violation. Last session, the committee decided to solve
the problem of elver dealers who have been convicted of an elver violation continuing to
benefit from the fishery by having other companies use their property in a different manner, so the Department does not believe that this prohibition was intended to remain.
Thank you for your consideration, and I would be happy to answer any questions you might have.
